newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA STOCKS SEEN WEAK AMID RUPIAH FALLS.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA STOCKS SEEN WEAK AMID RUPIAH FALLS.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen remaining weak on Tuesday, with a fresh plunge in the rupiah against the dollar seen harming sentiment, brokers said.
"Players are likely to remain sidelined on worries over these fresh falls," one broker said.
The Indonesian rupiah tumbled to 2,646/49 against the dollar at 0145 GMT on Tuesday from an opening of 2,610/20 on falls in the Malaysian ringgit and the Singapore dollar, dealers said.
On Monday, the Jakarta composite index fell 17.27 points, or 2.56 percent, to close at 658.17 points.
Brokers, however, said bargain hunting was likely in some blue-chips but volumes were likely to be limited due to worries over the rupiah.
